# ###############################################################################
# ############## Getting climatic and soil predictors ###########################
# Packages

```{r}
# Install 'soilDB' if not already installed
# install.packages('soilDB')

# Load libraries
library(readxl)       # To read Excel files
library(sp)           # For spatial data structures
library(raster)       # To work with raster data
library(foreach)      # For parallel processing
library(doParallel)   # For parallel backend registration
library(tidyverse)    # For data manipulation and visualization
library(Hmisc)        # For correlation and statistical functions
library(corrplot)     # For correlation matrix plotting
library(skimr)        # For summarizing data
library(openxlsx)     # For writing Excel files
```

# Load data 
Load data and translate as coordinates. 
```{r}
env <- read_xlsx("data/data_ferns.xlsx", sheet = "e_matrix")

coords <- data.frame(x = env$Long, y = env$Lat) %>%
  `rownames<-`(env$Site) %>%
  SpatialPoints(., proj4string = CRS('+proj=longlat +datum=WGS84 +no_defs'))

```
# Climatic variables rasters
# Wordclim data
We selected three climatic variables:
- bio_12 = Annual Precipitation (AP);
- bio_15 = Precipitation Seasonality (PS);
- bio_10 = Max Temperature of Warmest Month (MT);

```{r}
bio <- geodata::worldclim_global(
  path = "gis/worldclim",
  var = "bio",
  res = 2.5,
  download = T
)

names(bio)

x_var <- bio[[c('wc2.1_2.5m_bio_12', 'wc2.1_2.5m_bio_15', 'wc2.1_2.5m_bio_10')]]
names(x_var) <- c("AP", "PS", "MT")
x_var[[1]]
```

# Concatenate all climatic
Loop through selected rasters and extract values at site locations.

```{r}
clim <- foreach(i = 1:3) %do%
  {
    raster::extract(x = raster::raster(x_var[[i]]), y = coords)
  } |>
  do.call(what = cbind) |>
  `colnames<-`(c(
    "AP",
    "PS",
    "MT"
  )) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  mutate(id = env$Site)
```
# Soil variables rasters
Download soil data from SoilGrids (topsoil: 0-5 cm depth). Variables: 
- clay content (C);
- nitrogen (N); 
- cation exchange capacity (CEC).
```{r}
# SoilGrid
soil <- soilDB::fetchSoilGrids(
  x = env,
  loc.names = c("Site", 'Lat', 'Long'),
  depth_intervals = "0-5",
  variables = c("clay", "nitrogen", "cec")
)
# Select soil mean values and clean column names
var_soil <- dplyr::select(as.data.frame(soil), id, ends_with("mean")) %>%
  `colnames<-`(gsub(colnames(.), pattern = 'mean', replacement = ''))
```

# Merge variables
```{r}
bio <- merge(clim, var_soil, by = "id")
```
# Testing Multicolinearity

```{r}
# Rename columns to descriptive names
colnames(bio) <- c(
  'id',
  "Ann. Precipitation",
  "Prec. Seasonality",
  "Max. Temp.",
  "Clay",
  "Nitrogen",
  "CEC"
)
# Calculate correlation matrix and p-values
correl.b <- rcorr(as.matrix(bio[, -1]))
# Save correlation matrix to file
write.table(correl.b$r, "outputs/corr.txt")
write.xlsx(bio, "data/predictors.xlsx")


# Create summary table
# Generate summary statistics (mean, SD, etc.)
summary_var <- skim(bio[, -1]) |>
  mutate(
    skim_variable = c(
      "Annual Precipitation Mean (mm)",
      "Precipitation Seasonality (%CV)",
      "Max. Temperature in Warmest Month (C*100)",
      "Clay (g/100g)",
      "Nitrogen (cg/kg)",
      "Cation Exchange Capacity (cmol(c)/kg)"
    )
  )
# Save summary statistics to Excel
write.xlsx(summary_var, "outputs/summary_var.xlsx")

# Create and save a correlation plot (upper triangle only)
tiff(
  filename = "figs/correl.tiff",
  width = 180,
  height = 180,
  units = "mm",
  res = 600
)
corrplot(
  correl.b$r,
  type = "upper",
  method= 'number',
  order = "hclust",
  p.mat = correl.b$P,
  sig.level = 0.05,
  insig = "blank"
)

dev.off()
```
